cards.explanation: The answer is that the Ammonites exclaimed, “Aha!” God says, “Because you exclaimed, ‘Aha!’ when My sanctuary was profaned, when the land of Israel was laid waste, and when the house of Judah went into exile” (Ezekiel 25:3). One little word, and it's what God brings up. I think that's a word you want back the second it leaves your mouth.

The answer is camels, friends. God says, “I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels, and Ammon a resting place for sheep” (Ezekiel 25:5). Rabbah was a city, and God says it will become a camel pasture. Then the verse ends with “Then you will know that I am the LORD.”

The answer is True. Right after the camels and the sheep, God says, “Then you will know that I am the LORD” (Ezekiel 25:5). That line shows up again and again in this chapter. Whatever happens, God says they will know exactly who He is.

The answer is contempt, friends. God says, “Because you clapped your hands and stomped your feet and rejoiced over the land of Israel with a heart full of contempt” (Ezekiel 25:6). Contempt means looking down on somebody. Rejoicing over a neighbor's trouble while looking down on them is a heavy way to cheer.

The answer is False. God does not say the Ammonites keep their place. He says, “I will cut you off from the peoples and exterminate you from the countries. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD” (Ezekiel 25:7). I think this one is heavy, so it's worth reading slowly.

The answer is that Judah is like all the other nations. Moab and Seir said, “Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations” (Ezekiel 25:8). That's what God brings up. Then He says, “therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab” (Ezekiel 25:9). It was said out loud, and God heard it.

The answer is that they will no longer be remembered, friends. God says He will give Moab and the Ammonites to the people of the East, “so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations” (Ezekiel 25:10). It's a sobering line. A people that cheered over Judah's trouble ends up forgotten.

The answer is True. God says, “Because Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and in so doing incurred grievous guilt” (Ezekiel 25:12). Grievous is a serious word. God doesn't treat this as a small thing, and the verse says it plainly.

The answer is His people Israel, friends. God says, “I will take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel” (Ezekiel 25:14). Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and God names His people Israel as the hand He will use. It's His vengeance, carried out by the hand of Israel.

The answer is False. God says Israel “will deal with Edom according to My anger and wrath” (Ezekiel 25:14). It's His anger and wrath that sets the standard. Israel's own anger is not what the verse points to.

The answer is ancient, friends. God says the Philistines acted “with malice of soul to destroy Judah with ancient hostility” (Ezekiel 25:15). That hostility is called ancient. It's a heavy verse, and that one word says a lot.

The answer is the Cherethites. God says, “I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast” (Ezekiel 25:16). He names them right alongside the Philistines. It's a serious word from the Lord GOD, and it's good to know who's named.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “I will execute great vengeance against them with furious reproof. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance upon them” (Ezekiel 25:17). That's how the chapter closes. It's a heavy verse, and it's plainly there in the text.
